title: How a Vacuum Cleaner Works in 60 Seconds 🌀🧹 #shorts
description:
A vacuum cleaner doesn't really suck up dirt. A motor spins a fan tens of thousands of times a minute, throwing air out the back and leaving low pressure inside. Outside air rushes in through the nozzle to fill the gap, carrying dust with it, and a filter traps the dirt. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#vacuumcleaner #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: A vacuum cleaner doesn't really suck. The air outside *pushes* the dirt in.

steps.label: Motor & Fan
steps.text: An electric motor spins a *fan* more than twenty thousand times a minute.

steps.label: Low Pressure
steps.text: The fan throws air out the back, leaving *low pressure* inside the machine.

steps.label: Air Rushes In
steps.text: Room air rushes into the nozzle to fill the gap, and it carries the *dust* along.

steps.label: Brush Roll
steps.text: A spinning *brush* knocks dirt loose from the carpet, so the airflow can grab it.

steps.label: Filter
steps.text: A bin and *filter* trap the dirt, and clean air blows out the exhaust.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, low pressure, rush, *trap*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
